country.name: Philippines
country.listing_notice: Listing does not imply partnership or endorsement; actors are not ranked.
country.scope: Country snapshot and eight evidence-selected cities. Not a complete current national heat-exposure ranking, legal audit, full programme evaluation or exhaustive actor census.

evidence_definitions.concept: Designed, not yet tried by intended users.
evidence_definitions.reported: Described by implementers or reporting, without independent evaluation.
evidence_definitions.measured: Study, survey or analysis measured/analysed it.

heat_context.climate: Predominantly tropical maritime and humid. A hot dry rainfall season is not equivalent to a low-humidity hot-dry climate. Conditions vary by location and season.
heat_context.seasonality: PAGASA identifies a generally hot dry season in March–May; this is not a guarantee of safe temperatures in other months.
heat_context.night_heat: The National Adaptation Plan describes rising maximum and minimum temperatures, with minimum temperatures rising faster over the period discussed. Indoor night exposure is not measured by satellite surface temperature or a daytime station heat index.
heat_context.trend_scope: NAP climate discussion uses historical records, including 1951–2020 anomalies relative to 1991–2020; no historical trend is labelled a 2026 local measurement.

evidence.text: PAGASA describes high humidity and the broad seasonal pattern.
NAP discusses rising daytime and nighttime temperature indicators; no city-specific change rate extrapolated here.

plans_and_legal_basis.name: National Adaptation Plan 2023–2050
plans_and_legal_basis.published_fact: The national adaptation framework includes increased-temperature risks and sectoral responses; it is broader than a dedicated heat action plan.
plans_and_legal_basis.legal_limit: A strategic plan is not by itself proof of an appropriation, binding local operating trigger or completed intervention.

plans_and_legal_basis.name: Local disaster-management responsibilities
plans_and_legal_basis.published_fact: RA 10121 establishes local DRRM offices and planning/resource-management responsibilities.
plans_and_legal_basis.legal_limit: 2010 law is background legal context only here, not heat-outcome evidence. A heat-specific spend or action still needs an applicable approved local plan and budget. Current local-finance interpretation is checked separately.

warnings.national: PAGASA publishes heat-index information; DOST describes the iHeatMAP platform and localised heat information.
warnings.metric_limit: Heat index combines air temperature and humidity. It is not air temperature, indoor temperature, land-surface temperature or WBGT. Do not replace worksite exposure assessment with one public index.
warnings.last_mile: Online dissemination is documented. Reliable reach to people without smartphones, language/accessibility coverage, message receipt and funded action are not established by platform availability.

occupational_heat.binding_background: RA 11058 (2018) establishes private-sector OSH duties and worker rights, including duties to manage hazardous conditions; it excludes the public sector from its stated coverage.
occupational_heat.recent_update: PMAP circulated Labor Advisory 20, series 2026, on 27 October. Its accessible account describes workplace-specific risk assessment, rest/water/cooling and adjusting unsafe work.
occupational_heat.verification_boundary: DOLE live pages and original signed advisory were not retrieved. PMAP is an employer association describing its own circulation, not an independent legal determination. No new numeric threshold, wage entitlement, universal stop-work rule or exact WBGT limit is asserted here.
occupational_heat.income_and_voice: Whether rest is paid, which contractors/platform workers are covered, how grievances work and how protection is inspected need instrument- and workplace-specific verification.

sources.label: Republic Act 11058, occupational safety and health
PMAP circulation of DOLE signed advisory 20-2026

uncertainty.inferred: Worker-verified implementation and inspection can connect work protection to income resilience.
uncertainty.uncertain: Full 2026 operative texts, enforcement, informal-worker coverage and claims experience.

cooling_and_building_policy.limit: Coverage is conditional on occupancy/size and other rules; do not assume it covers every existing low-income dwelling. No cooling effect or health benefit is inferred from compliance alone.

cooling_and_building_policy.name: Refrigerant transition and servicing
cooling_and_building_policy.fact: UNIDO reports 2026 work with DENR/Philippine Ozone Desk on HCFC phase-out, future Kigali implementation and technical capacity for alternatives.
cooling_and_building_policy.limit: Do not conflate ozone-depleting HCFC phase-out with HFC phase-down. Equipment-specific refrigerant/GWP, charge limits, safety and recovery arrangements must be verified. No refrigerant retrofit is prescribed.

cooling_design_options.name: Envelope, shade and ventilation
cooling_design_options.evidence_scope: Researcher design interpretation, not a measured performance claim or endorsement.
cooling_design_options.mechanism: Reduce solar/radiant gain and use available air movement; ventilation must consider outdoor heat, air quality and clinical infection-control needs.
cooling_design_options.suits_why: Relevant in either climate; humid conditions limit what ventilation alone can achieve.
cooling_design_options.tradeoffs_and_upkeep: Roof strength/typhoon wind, fire, damp, safe access, tenancy permission and maintenance.

cost.note: No comparable local lifecycle cost quote verified. No USD or FX conversion is invented; a fund envelope is not a unit intervention cost.

source_context.label: Philippine Green Building Code 2015 original document via ADB

cooling_design_options.name: Efficient fans as a complementary option
cooling_design_options.evidence_scope: Researcher design interpretation, not a measured performance claim or endorsement.
cooling_design_options.mechanism: Move air around people rather than refrigerate the room.
cooling_design_options.suits_why: Benefit is conditional on humidity, air temperature, workload and vulnerability; not a universal safe-use prescription.
cooling_design_options.tradeoffs_and_upkeep: No power means no electric fan; repair and safe wiring matter. Do not infer illness prevention from comfort.

cost.note: No comparable local lifecycle cost quote verified. No USD or FX conversion is invented; a fund envelope is not a unit intervention cost.

cooling_design_options.name: Targeted air-conditioned refuges
cooling_design_options.evidence_scope: Researcher design interpretation, not a measured performance claim or endorsement.
cooling_design_options.mechanism: Provide a cooled indoor area; actual humidity control and heat-load performance must be checked.
cooling_design_options.suits_why: Refrigeration can cool in either climate; hot-humid design requires latent-load/humidity assessment.
cooling_design_options.tradeoffs_and_upkeep: Peak electricity, refrigerant leakage/GWP, street waste heat (loop cooling), outage vulnerability, queues, access and recurring cost.

cost.note: No comparable local lifecycle cost quote verified. No USD or FX conversion is invented; a fund envelope is not a unit intervention cost.

cooling_design_options.name: Maintained trees and public shade
cooling_design_options.evidence_scope: Researcher design interpretation, not a measured performance claim or endorsement.
cooling_design_options.mechanism: Intercept solar radiation and, where conditions permit, support evapotranspiration.
cooling_design_options.suits_why: Shade is useful in dry and humid settings; water, canopy and airflow influence results.
cooling_design_options.tradeoffs_and_upkeep: Water scarcity, storm damage, root space, irrigation upkeep, displacement and inaccessible paths; protect tenure and users.

cost.note: No comparable local lifecycle cost quote verified. No USD or FX conversion is invented; a fund envelope is not a unit intervention cost.

source_context.label: Philippine Green Building Code 2015 original document via ADB

cooling_design_options.name: Evaporative cooling screening
cooling_design_options.evidence_scope: Researcher design interpretation, not a measured performance claim or endorsement.
cooling_design_options.mechanism: Water evaporation can reduce dry-bulb temperature when sufficient evaporative potential exists.
cooling_design_options.suits_why: High humidity limits evaporation; no blanket recommendation for Philippine humid settings.
cooling_design_options.tradeoffs_and_upkeep: Additional humidity, water use, hygiene, indoor moisture and electrical/maintenance needs. Not a verified national programme.

cost.note: No comparable local lifecycle cost quote verified. No USD or FX conversion is invented; a fund envelope is not a unit intervention cost.

selection_method.rule: Combine named historical high population-exposure cities with a locally evidenced urban implementation case and regional heat-information/response and PAGASA station-extreme cases.
selection_method.historical_research: 2020 study covers 139 cities, largely using 2014–2016 hot-dry-season land-surface data and 2015 population indicators. Its exposure component is population density; it is not a current thermometer ranking.
selection_method.city_list_limit: These eight are evidence-selected priorities, not a verified national top-eight ranking in 2026. No comparable current dataset combining humidity, indoor/night heat, people exposed and vulnerability was verified.
selection_method.geographic_limit: Selected cases cover Luzon/Metro Manila and Mindanao; Visayas city coverage remains incomplete. That does not establish lower heat risk or less activity there.

gaps_in_evidence_collected: A consolidated, adopted national heat action plan with operational triggers, institutional mandates and itemised recurring finance was not verified; sectoral guidance and local initiatives were found.
Final adopted heat plans and heat-specific budget lines for most selected cities were not verified.
No independent outcome evaluation of the selected cooling-centre or awareness programmes was verified.
Indoor/night exposure, unpaid care, wage continuity, disability access and migrant/informal-worker reach remain incompletely documented in the reviewed sources.
No comparable local upfront/running/upkeep prices, poorest-quintile affordability assessment or heat-specific parametric policy wording verified.
No named worker-led or disability-led implementation partner was verified in this focused collection. This is not a claim that none exists.

equity_and_delivery_checks.scope: Researcher checks for local co-design, not measured claims about every Philippine programme.
checks: Include women and unpaid caregivers when schedules, access and household costs change.
Confirm accessible travel, entrances, toilets, seating and communication with disabled and older users; a designation does not establish accessibility.
Check whether renters can authorise roof work and whether improvements raise rents or displace users.
Include migrants, outdoor/informal workers and people without smartphones or cooling at home; verify who is actually reached.
Protect wage continuity and worker voice; do not use monitoring for surveillance, retaliation or unsafe output targets.
Budget drinking water, cleaning, servicing, electricity and replacement; account for outages and competing water use.
